context_spans.label: definition-algebraic-closure: an algebraic closure of F is a field extension of F that is algebraic over F and algebraically closed

standard_prerequisites: Context span 1169-1177: definition of algebraic closure
Same chapter: lemma-algebraic-goes-up (elements of an algebraic tower are algebraic down the tower, source cited in the proof); Zorn's lemma
core_obligations: Consider pairs (E, phi) with F subset E subset M a subextension and phi: E -> F-bar a morphism of F-extensions, ordered by extension of maps; a totally ordered family has the union map as upper bound, so Zorn gives a maximal (E, phi)
If E differs from M, pick alpha in M outside E; alpha is algebraic over E (lemma-algebraic-goes-up); let P be its minimal polynomial over E and P^phi its image in F-bar[x]
F-bar algebraically closed gives a root beta of P^phi; mapping x to beta extends phi to an F-embedding E(alpha) = E[x]/(P) -> F-bar, contradicting maximality; hence E = M
proof_roadmap: Set up the Zorn poset of partial embeddings
Take the maximal element and rule out a proper subextension
Adjoin one algebraic element and extend the embedding
